text:
sara: FYI I'm seeing a surge of 429s on the embeddings+rerank product lane starting ~09:05 UTC. Looks like queue depth shot up and admission control kicked in. dashboards: https://dash.redwood/ops/emb-rerank
noah: seeing this too, spans multiple regions but mostly eu-west-1. latencies for rerank requests jump to 1.2s p95 and then they get throttled.
kevin: are we sure it's single shared pool for both endpoints? I thought embeddings were routed to the quantized T4 pools and rerank to A100s, but maybe we collapsed during autoscaler shortage.
anya: current config: both endpoints use the "embed-rerank-shared" nodepool by default for cost reasons. Rerank is heavier per-request (cross-encoder), so it's starving the continuous small-embedding QPS.
sara: infra-bot posted an alert at 09:12: 

infra-bot: [ALERT] queue_depth(emb-rerank-shared) > 120 for 3m, admission_rate decreased to maintain GPU SLOs

noah: quick triage shows most 429s are rerank requests from a handful of large tenants. one tenant spiked 8x regular traffic.
kevin: can we implement separate capacity lanes? e.g. lane-A: embeddings (high QPS, low per-token cost, quantized) and lane-B: rerank (low QPS, high mem, reserved A100s). admission control per lane.
anya: agreed. Implementation notes: 1) split nodepool and route by endpoint + model profile 2) add per-lane admission tokens and rate limit derived from current GPU capacity 3) allow burst via short lived token bucket that charges quota if used
sara: that maps to the admission control model we've discussed before. We need rate limits tied to capacity: rate_limit = floor(gpu_slots * slot_throughput / cost_per_request).
kevin: can we make cost_per_request an estimate in the model descriptor so autoscaler and router can compute admission windows without hitting the backend? something like: model_profile: {cost_factor: 4.2, max_ctx: 2048}

noah: quick prototype I ran locally:
```
# admission calc (pseudo)
gpu_slots = 8
slot_throughput = 12.5  # reqs/sec per slot for tiny-embed
cost_factor = 0.75  # embed quantized
rate_limit = floor(gpu_slots * slot_throughput / cost_factor)
```

noah: embedding lane gets much higher absolute RPS with same GPUs. rerank lane uses cost_factor ~ 8-12 depending on model.
anya: operationally we also need cross-region constraints. eu-west doesn't have many A100s in our provider pool. If rerank lane in eu-west is starved, router should fallback to a remote region if latency budget allows, otherwise queue or send explicit 429 with retry-after.
sara: fallback is fine but we must be careful about data residency customers. For them we must queue rather than cross-region route. add tenant-level residency flag.
kevin: what about pre-warming dedicated lanes for top customers? Reserved small A100 pool per-big-tenant would avoid noisy neighbor. Tradeoff is cost. Estimate: one reserved A100 can cover ~250 rerank reqs/min at p95 target, cost delta ~$7k/month.
noah: alternative: soft reservation using priority tiers + ephemeral burst capacity. cheaper because that's autoscaler bursts, but can fail under sustained load.

anya: proposed short term plan: 1) split nodepool in k8s into embed-lane and rerank-lane (apply feature flag) 2) add model_profile.cost_factor to catalog + admission calculator in router 3) implement per-lane token bucket in front of worker pools that consults cluster_capacity metric 4) route large-tenants to dedicated lanes or apply stricter quotas
sara: urgent action: create INF-4132 to split pools and INF-4133 to add cost_factor to catalog and admission logic. Can someone own INF-4132 today?
kevin: I'll take INF-4132. I'll start with k8s changes and nodepool templates. Expect first PR by EOD.
noah: I'll own INF-4133 (catalog + router). I'll mock cost_factors based on bench runs and adapt after telemetry.
anya: I'll update oncall runbook to surface clearer 429 semantics and add queries to the embeddings dashboard: queue_depth_by_lane, admission_rate_by_tenant, rate_limit_calc.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: router/admission-controller v2 -> staging (canary)

kevin: quick note — when splitting pools we must update the autoscaler policy so embed-lane uses aggressive scale-to-zero for cost. rerank-lane should have reserved_min:1 in eu-west for hourly patterns.
sara: documentation and customer comms: we should send an email to customers using rerank heavy workloads explaining short term throttling and upcoming lanes. kevin can you draft?
kevin: will draft and share in #customer-success.

noah: one more thing: metrics to track post-change: p99 latency by lane, 429 rate by tenant, GPU utilization by lane, cross-region fallback count, and cost per 1M rerank tokens.
anya: ack. I'll add them to the dashboards and set alerts for >3% 429 sustained.
sara: thanks everyone. We'll aim to roll to prod next week behind feature flag, monitor canary, then flip for EU. If anything spikes ping @sara and @noah. :thumbsup:
